benefits: Instantly finds slope, equation, intercept, distance, midpoint and angle from any two points.
Handles vertical lines and identical points gracefully instead of crashing or showing NaN.
Perfect for students checking algebra and geometry homework.
Shows the full line equation in proper y = mx + b form.
Runs entirely in your browser — no data ever leaves your device.

faqs.a: A vertical line has x2 − x1 = 0, and division by zero is undefined in mathematics. The calculator detects this and reports the slope as undefined, giving the equation in x = a form instead.
faqs.q: Why is the slope of a vertical line undefined?

faqs.a: A positive slope means the line rises left to right; negative means it falls. A slope of 2 means y increases by 2 for every 1 unit x increases. A slope of 0 means the line is perfectly horizontal.
faqs.q: What does the slope value actually tell me?

faqs.a: If the slope is m and the line passes through (x1, y1), the intercept is b = y1 − m·x1. The calculator shows it automatically — for y = 2x + 3 the y-intercept is 3.
faqs.q: How do I find the y-intercept from the slope?

faqs.a: Check whether the line rises or falls, whether the two points are distinct, and whether you subtracted in the same order top and bottom: (y2 − y1)/(x2 − x1). Mixing up the order is the most common mistake.
faqs.q: My textbook answer differs — what should I check?

faqs.a: Yes — the distance uses the Pythagorean theorem on the differences in x and y, which is the same formula as the distance between any two points in the plane.
faqs.q: Is the distance just the Pythagorean theorem?

slope-calculator.formula:
Slope:  m = (y2 − y1) / (x2 − x1)

Line equation:  y = mx + b,  where b = y1 − m·x1 (y-intercept)
Vertical line (x1 = x2):  x = x1   (slope undefined)

Distance:  d = √((x2 − x1)² + (y2 − y1)²)
Midpoint:  ((x1 + x2)/2, (y1 + y2)/2)
Angle with x-axis:  θ = atan2(y2 − y1, x2 − x1)
howTo: Enter the coordinates of the first point (x1, y1).
Enter the coordinates of the second point (x2, y2).
Read the slope — the headline result — at the top of the results.
Check the full line equation, y-intercept, distance, midpoint and angle below.
If the points form a vertical line, the tool reports the slope as undefined with the equation x = a.
keyFacts: Slope is rise over run: m = (y2 − y1) / (x2 − x1).
A vertical line (x1 = x2) has an undefined slope — division by zero.
A zero slope means a perfectly horizontal line, y = constant.
Parallel lines share the same slope; perpendicular lines have slopes whose product is −1.
The distance between the points comes from the Pythagorean theorem applied to Δx and Δy.

limitations: Only works with straight lines — it cannot fit curves or find tangents.
Results are rounded for display; very long decimals may lose the last digits.
Coordinates are limited to ±1,000,000 to keep the arithmetic safe.
This finds the line through two points; it does not do regression through many points.
